title: Free UI Cards (light variant): white header-image card and full-bleed red/blue card
attribution_visible_in_image: Visible text: 'Free UI Cards', Figma logo, 'figma.com/@Spline', 'spline.one'. Likely the publisher; not confirmed.
contains_third_party_content: Photos of people; an Adobe logo inside the company chip. The upload filename was 'Figma Design System'.

observed.layout: Two 'Creative Director' cards on a light-grey page. Left: white card with a warm blurred-gradient header, avatar overlapping with a green online dot, 'Adobe Co.' chip, name 'Alex Turner', role, bookmark button, an outlined stat strip (star 5.0 Rating, flag $160 hours, clock 24 Month), and a black 'Get In Touch' bar. Right: full-bleed red/blue gradient card with a dark silhouette, glass chips and stat panel, white 'Get In Touch' bar. Branding: 'Free UI Cards', Figma logo, 'figma.com/@Spline', 'spline.one'.
observed.hierarchy: Name, then the CTA, then the stat strip.
observed.typography: Neutral grotesk; bold names, small grey roles. Unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Left: solid white with gradient header. Right: gradient photo with glass overlays.

implementation_notes: Glass chips on the right card use backdrop blur and low-alpha white.
interpretation.caveat: Stats read '$160 / hours' and '24 / Month'; intended meaning probably rate per hour and 24 months of experience, but the labels as written are ambiguous.

concept_work.essence: One card structure with a clean skin and an expressive skin.
what_makes_it_work: Overlapping avatar ties header and body.
gaps_to_make_it_work: Role text on the white card measures about 2.1-2.2:1.
Small light labels on the red card measure about 2.4-2.5:1.

links: Chip, role and stats together express credentials before the CTA.
Both skins share structure so the CTA stays in the same place.

approach: Backdrop-filter glass chips on the gradient skin
Token flip for text and CTA colors

pattern.name: One card structure, two skins (header image vs full-bleed)
use_when: Talent or people marketplaces with a single contact CTA
avoid_when: Backgrounds are unpredictable and no scrim is possible
must_preserve: Scrim behind text on gradients or photos
adaptation_examples: Freelancer card: '$160 / hour' and '24 mo experience'.
Speaker card: stats become talks and rating.
failure_modes: Light grey role text on white
Light text on saturated red near 2.5:1

lessons: Make value and label read as one phrase ('$160 / hour').
Keep the CTA constant when changing the skin.

related.relation: same series; this record shows a light skin on the left card
same series with different content and chips

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Neutral page; saturated red/blue only in the right card; CTA is black on the white card and white on the gradient card.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: A hire/contact card with credentials and a clear CTA.
Two clean skins with a stable layout.
Card conventions are followed, but stat labels are ambiguous.
One CTA is clear; bookmark and chip behavior unspecified; no hover or disabled states.
Same spacing, radii and component layout across both cards.
Two skins on one structure is useful but familiar.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 15.57:1; secondary text min 2.12:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
